prompt: Mid-case: A gym chain wants to grow revenue. You've found that membership is flat at 50,000, but revenue per member rose 8% thanks to personal training. You also learned the gyms are open 24 hours. You haven't looked at new locations. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: membership is flat at 50,000 at our 24-hour gyms, and personal training raised revenue per member 8%. Next, new locations.
options.feedback: Opening hours aren't part of what you found about growth, so they don't belong in the summary.

options.text: So far: membership grew 8% thanks to personal training. New locations come next.
options.feedback: It misstates what you found: membership is flat; revenue per member rose 8%.

options.text: So far: membership is flat at 50,000, so growth came from personal training, which raised revenue per member 8%. Next I'd look at new locations.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open.

options.text: So far: personal training is driving growth, so new locations won't be needed.
options.feedback: It closes a question that hasn't been looked at: new locations.

explanation: Known: membership is flat at 50,000, and personal training raised revenue per member 8%. Open: new locations. Next: evaluate them. If personal-training uptake is leveling off, new locations become the main growth lever.

irrelevant_facts: The chain's gyms are open 24 hours.
